reviews.review:
I absolutely LOVED the first Mass Effect, and I got through the first 3 and was very much anticipating playing this one, expecting it to be a huge upgrade. It's not. lol

It's on sale for 8 right now. More than worth that. In the end, it's still a Mass Effect game and you will probably like it if you enjoyed any of the other 3.
Has some bugs and downsides (e.g. writing isn't on par with the original trilogy), but the overall impression is good so far and the visuals + combat are great!

An often unfairly maligned game that came as the result of publisher meddling and studio mismanagement, but given a fair shot, the game stands fairly strong, particularly in comparison to the first game of the original trilogy. It's not fair to compare this game to all three of the original games, so when looking at it in comparison to Mass Effect, it's a fairly strong start to another game that started off fairly strong but not without its own troubles. 

The improvements to graphics and quality of life and gameplay have helped get this game closer to its full potential, with a story that presents a new mystery and gives us a chance to start playing as a nobody instead of a somebody. This hero's journey is a great one to follow as you try to navigate difficult decisions that don't align themselves so easily into a Good or Bad dichotomy that, while fun in the original trilogy, could lend itself to less thoughtful gameplay.

The game is not without its criticisms, as many of the side characters are generally easy to like but also easy to dislike too, particularly the romance options (but let's be real, the krogans are the best and we can't actually hate them because they're amazing). They are complicated and layered characters that sometimes get underwritten. The main story also, while interesting, doesn't feel like it has the same oomph, as players in the original Mass Effect game were combating the Geth only to see a larger plot afoot revealed piece by piece. 

I still hold out a small glimmer of hope that we will see a continuation of this story, as it has room to really develop into something great.

Not a great start. I've heard the tales of ME:A, the dead fish eyes, some of the bugs, sub-par designs for such a highly budgeted and hyped up game. However, I figured they would have fixed some of the more major issues after so many years. Instead with in the hour of starting, I get the infinite shuttle loading screen. I'll give this another chance, but I'm already tempted to free up space in my hard drive and just hit ME:1 on a higher difficulty.  

At the moment, I am giving this game a recommendation, because I understand that game creation is not easy and when you throw in the internet and many branching paths, it just gets more difficult. I want to give the people who worked on this a chance, even if EA benefits from it, but that will change quickly if I can't even land on Habitat 7.
